A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social support, as measured by social network size and satisfaction with social support, is an important factor to be considered in the care and support of patients with cancer.
social network size is an important variable to consider in understanding the role of social factors in the well-being of women with breast cancer and their parent caregivers.
the social environment plays a significant role in the psychological well-being of cancer patients, with the social network and social support being important variables in this regard.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social support is a complex concept with many dimensions that may be differentially important for various subgroups of cancer patients.
the quality of social support is a critical variable to consider when determining the relative importance of the size of the social network in relation to health and well-being.
the role of social networks and social support is complex and requires careful delineation and measurement in order to be able to draw appropriate clinical conclusions.
